newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dike breach threatens more floods in east Germany.
newsitem.headline: Dike breach threatens more floods in east Germany.

text.p: German border authorities said on Wednesday a flood barrier holding back the swollen Oder River near the village of Hohenwutzen had broken and would be impossible to repair.
Sirens sounded warning a further 9,000 inhabitants to prepare to evacuate the low-lying Oderbruch area, which officials said earlier could be flooded within hours if the dike at Hohenwutzen broke.
A spokesman for border control authorities in Frankfurt an der Oder confirmed reports by border guards at the scene that the dike had no longer been able to contain the immense pressure of the river.
"It (the water) is running," said the spokesman, adding that military helicopters were trying to block holes in the dike by dumping sand onto the flood barricades.
Guards at the scene said the area immediately threatened by the dike break was the northern-most swathe of the Oderbruch, the fertile plain lying north of Frankfurt an der Oder.

Earlier, floods showed signs of receding after a fresh high-water surge expected overnight did not materialise, although officials had said many flood-barriers were extremely porous and riddled with weak spots.
